title: From Two Metered AI Bills to One Claude Subscription | vitalii.no
description:
How an interview-coaching app's live hints moved off two metered cloud AI accounts and onto a single existing subscription — with an automatic fallback so a live session never just stalls.

Ghost Interviewer's live coaching loop ran its hints and follow-up questions through two separate metered cloud AI providers, billed per token on every practice interview, every streamed hint, every retry after a rate limit. Juggling two providers meant two sets of quotas, two failure modes, and two places pricing could quietly change without warning.

The app's generation and streaming endpoints were rewired to call Claude directly, authenticated with the same subscription used for everyday coding work, with a same-commit fallback to a faster tier when the main model is rate-limited so a live interview keeps moving instead of failing outright. The streaming protocol the frontend consumes stayed identical, so no UI code had to change.

The coaching loop now runs entirely on one existing subscription instead of two metered cloud accounts — one provider, one auth path, one place where quota and pricing live, down from two.
